title: Goroutine Leaks & Race Detector in Go

scenes.say: Ever wondered if goroutines can leak memory? And how you'd spot them before your interview?

scenes.label: Leak
scenes.sub: Goroutine leaks happen when they're blocked or can't exit.
scenes.say: Goroutine leaks happen when they're blocked or can't exit, often from a stuck channel or missing cancellation.
Leaks silently use memory, while races cause unsafe access. The race detector helps you spot data races in your code.

scenes.title: Race Detector
scenes.say: Run the race detector during development. It shows exactly where data races happen, so you can fix them fast.

scenes.question: What's a common goroutine leak cause?
scenes.right: Leaving goroutines blocked on channels or missing cancellation logic.
scenes.say: Interviewers love asking what causes goroutine leaks. It's usually blocked channels or missing cancellation.
